title: In repos/activity-api/src/services/exemplar-selector.ts, supply selected_at on the failure-side exemplar insert, matchin
description:
In repos/activity-api/src/services/exemplar-selector.ts, supply selected_at on the failure-side exemplar insert, matching the repair already landed on the success-side insert above it.

The file contains exactly one occurrence of this fragment:
success: false, digest_id: $digest_id, org_id: 'public' }

Replace it with exactly this:
success: false, digest_id: $digest_id, org_id: 'public', selected_at: time::now() }

One file, one op. Change nothing else on that line, no other line, and no other file.

WHY. The field is declared DEFINE FIELD selected_at ON execution_exemplar TYPE datetime VALUE $value OR time::now(). The VALUE clause is meant to default the timestamp when the caller omits it, but on this INSERT INTO form it does not apply, so the field arrives NONE and fails its own datetime type check. Measured on the live substrate 2026-09-10: 89 consecutive insert rejections in a single sweep, each logged as Found NONE for field selected_at, with record execution_exemplar:..., but expected a datetime, and execution_exemplar held 0 rows as a result.

The success-side insert on the line above has already been repaired the same way and is landed. Leaving this one unrepaired means the extraction stage retains only successful executions and silently discards every failure exemplar, which are the counter-examples the learning loop needs most.

Supplying the value explicitly satisfies the declared type rather than relying on a default that is demonstrably not firing.
